title: What makes Ooma AirDial® stand out as the leading POTS line replacement solution
summary: Learn how to audit nurse call systems for POTS dependencies and plan a reliable transition from aging copper lines.
body_markdown:
As the leader of Solution Engineering at Ooma, I spend every day talking with customers across a wide range of industries. One question comes up more than any other: What makes AirDial different?


It’s a great question. With more POTS replacement solutions on the market than ever before, it’s important to note that not all solutions are created equally. Here’s what sets AirDial apart, and why organizations trust AirDial to support their most critical communications, including life-safety applications.


## Designed different. Built better.


Let’s start with the biggest difference: we designed AirDial from the ground up.


Unlike many POTS replacement solutions that piece together hardware, connectivity, cloud services, and management tools from multiple vendors, AirDial is a single, end-to-end platform developed entirely by Ooma. From the hardware and cloud telephony to Remote Device Management and ongoing software innovation, we own the full stack.


The result is a purpose-built solution for mission-critical fire, life safety, and emergency communications—delivering greater reliability, simpler management, and continuous innovation from one trusted vendor.


## Designed to improve


Since we designed AirDial, we don’t wait for anyone else to innovate. We continuously update AirDial so you get new features, enhancements, and performance improvements—keeping AirDial at the forefront of POTS replacement without requiring new hardware.


Our roadmap is driven by people who use AirDial every day. We listen to our customers and partners, prioritize what matters most, and keep making the industry’s leading POTS replacement solution even better.


## Built-in compliance


When life-safety systems are involved, compliance isn’t optional. AirDial is engineered to support the stringent requirements of mission critical communications, helping organizations replace legacy POTS lines with confidence while maintaining compliance with key industry codes and standards.


AirDial is built with NFPA 72 and ASME A17.1 requirements in mind and is certified to UL 864 and UL 62368-1 standards. It is also approved by the California State Fire Marshal and the New York City Fire Department for fire alarm communications. Combined with its secure MFVN architecture and support for regulations such as Kari’s Law, RAY BAUM’S Act, HIPAA, and PCI, AirDial provides a trusted foundation for today’s most critical communications.


## Device management that goes beyond monitoring


AirDial’s Remote Device Management (RDM) goes far beyond basic monitoring. From a single dashboard, you get complete visibility into every connected device, with real-time alerts, call activity, LTE signal strength, battery health, and device status all in one place.


AirDial instantly alerts you when equipment is disconnected, a line is left off hook, or calls are made from specific devices like elevator phones and emergency call boxes. Exclusive capabilities like equipment disconnect detection and extended off-hook alerts help you identify issues before they become service disruptions. It is proactive intelligence that helps you prevent outages, reduce service calls, and keep critical systems online.


AirDial’s built-in LCD screen gives onsite teams immediate visibility into LTE signal strength, battery power, and phone line status, helping them pinpoint issues and act quickly.


## Patented network path reliability


Mission-critical communication deserves more than a single point of failure. AirDial’s patented MultiPath Technology (MPT) was designed to be fail-safe, not failover. Instead of waiting for one connection to fail before switching to another, every call is transmitted simultaneously over both LTE and Ethernet. If one path experiences an outage, congestion, or degraded performance, the other continues carrying the call without interruption.


This active-active architecture delivers a higher level of resilience than conventional failover solutions, helping ensure reliable communications for fire alarm panels, elevator emergency phones, security systems, emergency call boxes, and other mission-critical analog devices when they matter most.


## Recognized industry leadership


AirDial continues to earn recognition from leading industry organizations for innovation, reliability, and customer value. Recent honors include the Frost & Sullivan Best Practices Leader in POTS Replacement (2025 and 2026, Elevator World Ellie Award (2025), ChannelVision Visionary Spotlight Award (2026), TMC Internet Telephony Product of the Year (2026), and the Merit Gold Award for Security & Cloud Services (2026). We didn’t earn these awards by following the market. We earned them by leading the market.


## Support for any analog communication device


Replacing your POTS lines shouldn’t mean replacing your equipment. AirDial is designed to support any device that relies on an analog telephone line, allowing you to modernize your communications while preserving your existing infrastructure.


From fire alarm panels and elevator emergency phones to security systems, access control, fax machines, paging systems, blue light phones, building automation equipment, and more, AirDial delivers a seamless transition without the cost and disruption of a rip and replace project. In fact, we have yet to encounter an analog device that AirDial could not support.


## Flexible deployment and procurement options


Every organization has unique deployment, procurement, and budget requirements. AirDial is designed to adapt to your environment with flexible implementation options, including self-installation, guided deployment, or turnkey project management delivered by Ooma’s deployment experts.


Procurement is just as flexible. Organizations can choose the purchasing model that best fits their needs, including CapEx or OpEx options, while government agencies and public sector organizations can streamline purchasing through Carahsoft and its available contract vehicles. Whether you’re deploying at a single location or across thousands of sites, AirDial provides flexibility to scale with your organization.


## One vendor. One platform. One monthly bill.


Replacing POTS lines shouldn’t mean juggling multiple vendors, disconnected technologies, and separate invoices. AirDial brings everything together in one fully integrated solution that includes the hardware, cloud telephony, LTE connectivity, Remote Device Management, and expert support.


With Ooma as your single partner, you get one team to support you and one predictable monthly bill. It’s a simpler, more reliable approach that eliminates complexity and delivers everything you need from a single trusted provider.


## Conclusion


The more you compare POTS replacement solutions, the clearer the differences become. AirDial wasn’t assembled from off-the-shelf components or adapted from existing technology. We designed it, manufactured to our specifications, and because we own the entire platform, we continue to advance it.


From patented MultiPath Technology (MPT) reliability and advanced Remote Device Management to built-in compliance, flexible deployment, and continuous innovation, every part of AirDial was engineered to deliver a higher standard for mission critical communications.


It’s no coincidence that other providers compare themselves to AirDial. When you’re the company setting the standard, everyone else is measured against you. Look beyond the hype and compare what really matters. We think you’ll see why organizations across every industry continue to choose AirDial and why it remains the leader in POTS replacement.
